issue.title: Runner module imports overwrite the process SIGTERM handler
issue.description: Proposed by sase-1rq.2.1.4.1.1 note #2 and independently by sase-1rq.2.1.4.1.3 note #9. At 539afb211e, importing sase.axe.run_agent_runner changes signal.getsignal(SIGTERM) from SIG_DFL to install_sigterm_handler._handler; line 87 installs soft=True at import. mentor_runner.py line 30 likewise installs a handler at import. Install handlers only in the owned runner entry lifecycle, preserving early production signal handling and existing shutdown semantics; imports must not replace the caller handler. Add fresh-interpreter import and real-entry signal tests. Root cause is precise; small scope. Search of all-status tasks and recent tasks found no duplicate; the global-state epic is topical, not the origin of these older side effects.

task_type_fields.impact: Any importing process, including pytest workers, inherits runner-specific signal behavior and can ignore termination.
task_type_fields.repro: In a fresh interpreter, capture signal.getsignal(signal.SIGTERM), import sase.axe.run_agent_runner, and compare: SIG_DFL becomes a soft handler. Seen in monitors kyhnsmgpcjx9 and aa3fzgn042n3 as swallowed SIGTERM.

issue.creation_reason: Contention phases exposed a pre-existing import side effect that makes signal tests order-dependent and can defeat worker teardown. Landing review independently reproduced the handler replacement.
